issues.description: The problem statement and template declare a public method singFarmSong() on Farm, but the solution implementation provides a method named playFarmSong() instead of singFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch means code or tests that expect singFarmSong() will not find an implementation in the solution, preventing students from reconciling template instructions with the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the public API: rename the solution's playFarmSong() method to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to playFarmSong(), so the method name expected by the problem statement and template is implemented in the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and template specify a public Farm method named 'singFarmSong()', but the solution implementation uses the name 'playFarmSong()' for the same functionality. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) breaks the direct mapping students expect between the assignment description, the starter code, and the reference solution and may cause confusion or failing tests that look for 'singFarmSong()'.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method 'playFarmSong()' to 'singFarmSong()' (and update any calls in Main or elsewhere) so the method name matches the problem statement and the template; alternatively, rename the template and problem references to 'playFarmSong()' if changing the solution is not possible — prefer aligning to 'singFarmSong()' to preserve the assignment wording.
